scope: Stage 2: local landscape settings and small enclosed water bodies. Existing broad world geography stays authoritative. No volcano, cave, waterfall or other landmark catalogue expansion; stage 3 tree art remains separate.

sources.title: USGS: What Is a Desert?
sources.design: Dryness does not imply a sand sea. Preserve extensive gravel, bare rock and sparse-cover settings alongside sandy provinces.

sources.title: USGS: Types of Deserts
sources.design: Climate and geographical context distinguish hot, cold, rain-shadow and coastal deserts. Ground materials are an independent axis of variation.

sources.title: NPS: Aeolian Landforms
sources.design: Dunes require available loose sediment as well as wind and limited stabilising cover. Coherent sand availability gates dune relief; desert is not a universal dune switch.

sources.title: USGS: Great Sand Dunes
sources.design: Dune fields can coexist with extensive sand sheets. Model accumulation provinces rather than covering every sandy surface with identical ridges.

sources.title: EPA: Classification and Types of Wetlands
sources.design: Distinguish open herbaceous marshes, woody swamps and organic peatlands; their saturation, soil chemistry and vegetation differ. Wetlands need not be flooded continuously.

sources.title: NPS: Kettles
sources.design: Glacial deposits support enclosed depressions that may hold small lakes or ponds. Water must occupy a basin rather than a plane crossing an arbitrary hillside.

sources.title: USGS: Geology of the Loess Hills, Iowa
sources.design: Windblown silt supports a distinct rolling/dissected landscape; it is different from dune sand and exposed hard bedrock.

sources.title: Alaska geological survey: Guide to Permafrost and Quaternary Geology
sources.design: Ice-rich lowlands can contain shallow thaw depressions and ponds. This pass uses static derived glacial/wet-lowland settings, without claiming a permafrost thaw simulation.

model_priors: Metre-scale wavelengths, material thresholds, pond encounter density, survey tolerances and depth ranges are tunable game-model priors. They are not direct archaeological or global hydrological measurements.
architecture: Continuous regional controls over shared terrain vertices; dry substrate includes regional relief before channel fitting. Sparse world-space pond candidates require a complete gentle rim survey; cut ground and water footprint are evaluated together. Bounded local caches, no global pond/entity tick ledger.
status: In progress. Core controls and actual generated-world pond/mesh tests pass; native visual/performance acceptance and regional coverage review still required. Selected NPC build slot-a remains unchanged.
